note: Golden season labels are the independent check on the engine: the months a person who knows the place would name, written down without consulting the engine's answer, so that a scoring change which quietly breaks a well-known destination has something to fail against. These were drafted by the coding agent from general knowledge and are NOT approved. The release gate needs status APPROVED and at least 30 cases. Status stays below APPROVED while any case is unsigned, because the file would otherwise claim an approval that does not exist. Reject freely: a label nobody stands behind is worse than no label. Never edit a label to make a test pass — that is the one change that destroys the whole point of the file.

labelSchema.slug: destination slug in the published catalogue
labelSchema.expectedMonths: months a knowledgeable walker would name; wrap-around and two-window seasons are just sets
labelSchema.label: the season in words, as it would be said out loud
labelSchema.basis: why those months and not others, and what closes the season
labelSchema.confidence: high where the season is a settled fact, medium where reasonable people would draw the line differently

cases.name: Dolomites, Italy
cases.label: mid-June to late September
cases.basis: The rifugio network opens around the third week of June and closes in the last days of September; before and after that the high traverses hold snow and there is nowhere to sleep.

cases.name: Chamonix, France
cases.label: late June to September
cases.basis: High balcony trails and cols clear of snow from late June; refuges close through September.

cases.name: Zermatt, Switzerland
cases.label: July to September
cases.basis: The walking season here is short and firmly mid-summer. The modelled cell sits at about 3,000 m, some 800 m above the Gornergrat and Sunnegga trail network where the walking actually happens, and at that height the persistent-snow hold is plausible. The engine currently offers no month at all for Zermatt, which is plainly wrong for the destination and quite possibly right for the cell.
cases.reviewNote: Kept as a standing challenge to the representative-cell choice. A label saying there is a season against an engine saying there is none is the most useful disagreement in this set; it should not be resolved by editing the label.
cases.approvalHeld: Unsigned on purpose. This is a case where the engine and the label disagree, which is the only kind that can fail the test. Signing it is a decision about whether the label or the engine is wrong, and it has not been made.

cases.name: Triglav, Slovenia
cases.label: June to September
cases.basis: Julian Alps huts run mid-June to late September; the via ferrata routes hold snow either side.

cases.name: High Tatras, Slovakia
cases.label: mid-June to September
cases.basis: The higher marked trails are formally closed from 1 November to 15 June, so regulation sets the season as much as weather does.

cases.name: Picos de Europa, Spain
cases.label: June to September
cases.basis: Snow lies late on the limestone massifs and the refuges run through summer; autumn brings Atlantic cloud onto the tops.

cases.name: Banff, Canada
cases.label: July to late September
cases.basis: Higher passes hold snow into early July; the larch turn in late September is the recognised end of the season.

cases.name: Rocky Mountain National Park, United States
cases.label: July to September
cases.basis: The alpine trails clear around the start of July; afternoon thunderstorms govern the day rather than the season.

cases.name: Glacier National Park, United States
cases.label: July to mid-September
cases.basis: Going-to-the-Sun Road usually opens late June or early July, and that opening is what makes the high trails reachable at all.

cases.name: Cairngorms, Scotland
cases.label: May to September
cases.basis: Walkable year-round by the experienced, but the plateau holds snow into May and the recognised hillwalking season is late spring to early autumn.

cases.name: Lake District, England
cases.label: May to September
cases.basis: No snow gate at these heights; the season is set by daylight and by how much rain a walker will accept.

cases.name: Snowdonia, Wales
cases.label: May to September
cases.basis: As the Lake District: rain and daylight rather than snow, with winter conditions on the ridges a specialist matter.

cases.name: Mallorca, Spain
cases.label: spring and autumn, avoiding high summer
cases.basis: The Serra de Tramuntana is walked either side of summer; July and August are too hot on exposed limestone.

cases.name: Amalfi Coast, Italy
cases.label: April to June and September to October
cases.basis: The coastal paths are exposed and unshaded; midsummer is uncomfortably hot.

cases.name: Lycian Way, Turkiye
cases.label: March to May and October to November
cases.basis: The long-distance route is walked in spring and autumn; summer on the Mediterranean coast is too hot for consecutive days of it.

cases.name: Cappadocia, Turkiye
cases.label: April to June and September to October
cases.basis: Continental plateau: hot summers, cold winters, and two comfortable shoulder windows in the valleys.

cases.name: Atlas Mountains, Morocco
cases.label: April to June and September to October
cases.basis: Snow on the high passes into spring, fierce heat in midsummer lower down; the season is the gap between the two.
cases.approvalHeld: Unsigned on purpose. This is a case where the engine and the label disagree, which is the only kind that can fail the test. Signing it is a decision about whether the label or the engine is wrong, and it has not been made.

cases.name: Kilimanjaro, Tanzania
cases.label: January to February and June to October
cases.basis: Two dry windows between the long rains of March to May and the short rains of November. The second window opens in June; an earlier draft of this label started it in July, which was simply wrong.
cases.reviewNote: Corrected during review. Flagged because the correction happens to move the engine from 'partly' to 'agrees', which is the direction a label should never be edited towards. The June start stands on the rainfall pattern alone, but weigh it knowing the engine's answer prompted the second look.

cases.name: Mount Kenya, Kenya
cases.label: January to February and July to September
cases.basis: The same two-rains pattern as Kilimanjaro, with the drier windows a little narrower.
cases.approvalHeld: Unsigned on purpose. This is a case where the engine and the label disagree, which is the only kind that can fail the test. Signing it is a decision about whether the label or the engine is wrong, and it has not been made.

cases.name: Simien Mountains, Ethiopia
cases.label: October to March
cases.basis: The Ethiopian highland rains run roughly June to September; the trekking season is the dry half of the year after them.

cases.name: Drakensberg, South Africa
cases.label: March to November, avoiding midsummer
cases.basis: The escarpment is walked from autumn through the dry, stable winter and into spring. What closes the season is midsummer, December to February, when violent afternoon thunderstorms make the high traverses dangerous. An earlier draft excluded the winter months, which is where some of the most settled walking is.

cases.name: Torres del Paine, Chile
cases.label: November to March
cases.basis: The austral summer is the only period the W and O circuits are fully serviced; outside it wind and cold close the passes.

cases.name: El Chalten, Argentina
cases.label: November to March
cases.basis: The same Patagonian summer as Torres del Paine, with wind rather than temperature as the limiting factor.
cases.approvalHeld: Unsigned on purpose. This is a case where the engine and the label disagree, which is the only kind that can fail the test. Signing it is a decision about whether the label or the engine is wrong, and it has not been made.

cases.name: Salkantay, Peru
cases.label: May to September
cases.basis: The Andean dry season. The wet season from December to March makes the high pass and the cloud-forest descent genuinely unpleasant.

cases.name: Annapurna, Nepal
cases.label: October to November, and March to April
cases.basis: The monsoon closes the circuit June to September and winter closes the high pass; October and November are the settled window, spring the secondary one. Note that the modelled cell sits at about 4,300 m, roughly 1,300 m above where most of the circuit is walked, so a disagreement here may be a fair description of a high pass rather than a wrong season. Treat it as a question about the cell as much as about the score.
cases.reviewNote: Label describes the trek; the cell describes a high pass. Kept deliberately, with the gap named.
cases.approvalHeld: Unsigned on purpose. This is a case where the engine and the label disagree, which is the only kind that can fail the test. Signing it is a decision about whether the label or the engine is wrong, and it has not been made.

cases.name: Langtang, Nepal
cases.label: October to November, and March to April
cases.basis: The same monsoon and winter bracket as Annapurna, at slightly lower altitude.
cases.approvalHeld: Unsigned on purpose. This is a case where the engine and the label disagree, which is the only kind that can fail the test. Signing it is a decision about whether the label or the engine is wrong, and it has not been made.

cases.name: Ladakh, India
cases.label: June to September
cases.basis: A high desert in the monsoon's rain shadow; the season is set by the passes being open and the nights being survivable, not by rain.

cases.name: Kumano Kodo, Japan
cases.label: March to May and October to November
cases.basis: The June to July rainy season and the humid typhoon-prone late summer bracket the two comfortable windows.

cases.name: Mount Rinjani, Indonesia
cases.label: May to October
cases.basis: The route is formally closed for much of the wet season, roughly January to March; the dry months are the trekking season.

cases.name: Tongariro, New Zealand
cases.label: November to April
cases.basis: Outside the austral summer the Alpine Crossing becomes an alpine undertaking requiring axe and crampons, which is a different activity.

cases.name: Routeburn, New Zealand
cases.label: late October to April, the Great Walk season
cases.basis: The Department of Conservation Great Walk season runs late October to April; outside it the huts are unserviced and avalanche risk is real.

reviewLog: Reviewed by the coding agent after drafting. Kilimanjaro's second dry window corrected to start in June. Drakensberg widened to include the dry winter, which the first draft wrongly excluded. Madeira dropped: the original label was wrong and any correction would have been shaped by having seen the engine's answer, which is not a label anyone should sign. Annapurna and Zermatt keep their labels with the cell elevation named in the basis, so their disagreements read as questions about the representative cell rather than about the season.
Still unapproved. A human operator has to sign each case before status becomes APPROVED.
approvalLog: 2026-09-06T11:11:24.233Z: ThorfinnThor approved, as a batch, the 25 cases the engine currently agrees with. Recorded honestly: this was a single instruction covering all of them, not 25 separate judgements.

The remaining 6 are held unsigned. They are the cases that disagree, and therefore the only ones that can make the test fail. Approving a set filtered to the cases that already pass would turn the golden labels into a mirror of the engine, which is the failure mode this file exists to prevent.
Zermatt and El Chalten: the engine offers no month at all. El Chalten and Zermatt are both persistent-snow holds on cells sitting well above the walking.
Atlas, Mount Kenya, Annapurna, Langtang: the engine's months run warmer or later than the label. Four of the six share one shape, a modelled cell higher than where people walk.
